source_name: НБРСМ — Закон за спречување перење пари и финансирање на тероризам (AML law page, cash-payment ceiling)
why_relevant: The AML law (Art. 204 as cited by practitioners) is the instrument that sets North Macedonia's cash-payment limit and its step-down schedule; central-bank hosting makes this a stable legal reference point.

source_name: Управа за финансиско разузнавање (Financial Intelligence Office, UFR)
why_relevant: The AML supervisor publishes the amending laws and guidance that define cash-payment prohibitions (including the virtual-asset cash threshold); primary regulator for cash-limit policy changes.

source_name: Управа за јавни приходи (UJP / Public Revenue Office) — fiscalisation section
why_relevant: The tax authority owns fiscalisation: the obligation to register every cash payment through approved fiscal devices, the rules on issuing fiscal receipts for card payments, and the inspection statistics on non-compliance — the operational core of cash-substitution enforcement.

source_name: УЈП — МојДДВ (MyVAT receipt-scanning cashback programme)
why_relevant: МојДДВ is the flagship de-cashing/formalisation incentive: citizens scan fiscal receipts for a VAT refund paid to a bank account. User counts, refund caps and quarterly payout announcements are a rare quantified proxy for receipt-issuance discipline and for account-based payout reach.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Стратегија за формализирање на неформалната економија 2023–2027
why_relevant: The national policy document on the informal economy; sets the government's own shadow-economy framing, measures and targets, which in this country are tightly bound to cash use, fiscalisation and card acceptance.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Акциски план за спроведување на стратегијата за формализирање на неформалната економија
why_relevant: The action plan names the concrete measures, owners and deadlines — the level at which mandatory card acceptance, fiscalisation upgrades and cash-limit steps actually appear.

source_name: Портал за развојни документи (portal.mdt.gov.mk) — Програма на економски реформи (ERP)
why_relevant: The annual Economic Reform Programme integrates the informal-economy strategy and states fiscal-revenue effects of formalisation; an EU-facing document, so it is unusually explicit about measurement and targets.

source_name: CEA (Center for Economic Analyses) — Shadow Economy in Macedonia study
why_relevant: Independent think-tank estimate of the shadow economy using national data; the classic non-government benchmark against which official informality figures are compared, and typically discusses cash-demand-based estimation methods.

source_name: Finance Think (Skopje economic research institute)
why_relevant: Cited in search results as the local think tank producing the working range for the size of the informal economy (roughly 21–34%, with later estimates up to ~40%); the most frequently quoted domestic authority on informality and therefore on cash intensity.

source_name: IMF — Shadow Economies Around the World (WP/18/17) and Europe's Shadow Economies
why_relevant: Cross-country shadow-economy estimates including North Macedonia (cited at ~37.6% of the economy); provides the comparable regional baseline and the currency-demand methodology that links cash in circulation to informality.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — North Macedonia
why_relevant: Supply-side series giving ATM and POS geographic/demographic outreach for North Macedonia on a comparable international basis — the standard measure of ATM network density (e.g. ~67 ATMs per 100k adults in 2023).

source_name: World Bank Open Data — ATMs per 100,000 adults, North Macedonia (FB.ATM.TOTL.P5)
why_relevant: Convenient API-addressable mirror of the FAS ATM-density indicator with a long time series, useful for trend charts on cash-access infrastructure; also the gateway to Global Findex demand-side cash/payment behaviour data.

source_name: FRED — Geographical Outreach: ATMs per 100,000 Adults for Macedonia (MKDFCAANUM)
why_relevant: Machine-friendly series endpoint for the same ATM-density metric; lowest-friction option for automated time-series collection when the IMF portal is awkward.

source_name: Државен завод за статистика (State Statistical Office) — household consumption survey
why_relevant: Household Budget Survey publications give the expenditure structure that any cash-versus-card share must be normalised against, and the SSO is the body that would carry informal-employment/undeclared-work indicators.

source_name: Nova Makedonija / Telma / Pari.com.mk — mainstream coverage of cash limits, cash preference and UJP fiscalisation controls
why_relevant: General media carry datapoints that are otherwise hard to surface: the stepwise cash-limit reductions (EUR 3,000 to 2,000 to 1,000), the reported persistence of cash preference over cards, and UJP's finding of fiscalisation irregularities at roughly a third of inspected entities.

source_name: Правдико / Nikola Mladenov (LinkedIn) / Pepeljugoski / Nova Konsalting — practitioner commentary on cash rules
why_relevant: Law and accounting practitioners publish the clearest operational reading of the cash rules — the MKD 6,000 per-transaction and MKD 60,000 monthly ceilings for legal entities, the EUR 1,000 general limit from 2025 and the EUR 500 virtual-asset cash limit, plus consumer-side fiscalisation duties. Useful for interpretation, never as the citation of record.

source_name: Unija.com — Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems + AML amendments briefing
why_relevant: Regional accounting/advisory group summarising the introduction of the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems together with the AML amendments — the pairing that drives both card-acceptance expansion and cash-limit tightening.

source_name: MDPI Economies — Rethinking Fiscal Decentralization in Relation to Regional Informality (European transition country)
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed work linking ICT/payment-infrastructure penetration to informality and arguing that promoting electronic transactions and reducing cash reliance raises fiscal revenue — directly on the cash-substitution causal question, with sub-national granularity.

source_name: Global Initiative SEE-Obs — North Macedonia illicit financial flows report
why_relevant: Covers illicit financial flows and cash-based value transfer in North Macedonia; a reveals-indirectly source for the part of cash demand that never appears in official informality statistics.

source_name: Bertelsmann BTI 2026 — North Macedonia country report
why_relevant: Recurring qualitative assessment that cites the domestic informal-economy range (roughly 21–40%) and frames it as a structural constraint; useful as a dated, citable secondary anchor and a pointer to the underlying local estimates.

source_name: Coface — North Macedonia country risk file
why_relevant: Commercial risk analysis that links the size of the informal economy to the narrow tax base; a fast, regularly refreshed secondary read on how the cash economy is perceived by commercial counterparties.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API — nbrm.mk /content/Platni sistemi/ archive
why_relevant: The Wayback CDX index returned dozens of archived NBRSM payment-systems artefacts, including the yearly 'Годишна информација за движењата во плаќањата во РМ/РСМ' PDFs for 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and Excel workbooks ('Годишен за веб МК.xlsx', 'Годишен извештај.xlsx'). Several of these live-site URLs have since 301'd/404'd, so the archive is the only route to superseded annual payment-statistics releases, older card/ATM/POS series and prior tariff/fee documents.

source_name: Wayback Machine — archived MK commercial bank tariff books and card fee pages (Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB, Halkbank etc.)
why_relevant: Bank tariff books ('Тарифник за надоместоци', 'Одлука за тарифа') and card/POS fee pages are routinely overwritten with each revision; the archive is the only way to build a time series of MK card issuing/acquiring fees, ATM withdrawal charges and POS merchant service charges. Same CDX pattern that proved productive on nbrm.mk should apply per bank domain.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics (PAY dataset, card-based payment transactions incl. cash withdrawals)
source_subtype: official statistical data portal / cross-country aggregator
why_relevant: Authoritative, methodologically harmonised comparator set for card payments, terminals (POS/ATM), transaction volumes and values across euro area and most non-euro EU members. North Macedonia is NOT an ECB reporter, so this is the benchmark layer used to normalise and interpret MK figures (e.g. cards per capita, POS density, transaction value per card) against BG/HR/RO/GR/SI peers. Bulk download and SDMX API available.

source_name: ECB Payments statistics methodological notes (definitions for card/terminal indicators)
why_relevant: Defines 'non-remote card payment', 'terminal', 'card with a payment function' etc. Needed to test whether NBRSM's MK definitions are comparable before any MK-vs-EU benchmark is asserted; prevents false conclusions from definitional mismatch.

source_name: CEIC Data — North Macedonia Payment System database
why_relevant: CEIC normalises and re-publishes MK payment-system series (ATM counts/density, payment system indicators) with source attribution and long history, in a machine-readable, comparably-coded form. Useful as a cross-check on NBRSM/State Statistical Office figures and to spot revisions or discontinuities.

source_name: Trading Economics — North Macedonia indicators (banking/money/financial block)
why_relevant: Fast, consistently-formatted mirror of MK macro-financial series (banks balance sheet, central bank balance sheet, deposit/lending rates, money supply, current account) with forecast overlays; handy for quick context around payments-market sizing and for change-detection when NBRSM publishes. Card/POS-specific series appear thin, so treat as macro context rather than payments-primary.

source_name: Statista Market Insights — Banking / Digital Payments outlook, North Macedonia
why_relevant: Modelled market-size and forecast estimates for MK banking and digital payments (transaction value, users, ARPU). Statista's MK numbers are largely modelled rather than observed, so they are valuable as a commercially-circulated benchmark that clients and competitors cite — and as a signal of what the market believes — rather than as a primary measurement.
